original_target.title: Are compact convex sets in arbitrary linear metric spaces absolute retracts?

full_original_statement:
Let $`E`$ be a metrizable topological vector space, without assuming local convexity, and let $`C\subset E`$ be compact and convex. Must $`C`$ be an **absolute retract**? That means that whenever $`C`$ is embedded as a closed subset of a metrizable space $`Y`$, there is a continuous retraction $`Y\to C`$.

The question asks for the absolute-retract property of every such $`C`$. It does not ask only whether continuous self-maps of $`C`$ have fixed points.

**Editorial clarification:** Make the intended nonempty compact-convex convention explicit.

sources.scope_comparison: TheoremA.7 claims every compact p-convex set in a Hausdorff TVS is AR, including p=1 and the nonempty metrizable target. However, its argument uses LemmaA.1's subordinate continuous partition with a unique dominant component everywhere. For K=[0,1], U1=[0,2/3), U2=(1/3,1], subordination forces phi1(0)=1 and phi1(1)=0, so continuity forces a tie. With any refinement a unique maximal index is locally constant and hence constant on K, forcing one proper cover member to contain K. The proposed proof therefore has an explicit unrepaired gap; this is not a counterexample to the AR target. Retain hold rather than certify a complete matching solution.
